findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional deque-and-running-sum design. Each next call appends once, expires at most one oldest value, updates the same total, and divides by the live length; the app adapter cleanly applies that native object over the stream. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 346 and its Python MovingAverage surface. The Reference preserves constructor capacity, next-call semantics, partial-window averaging, the app stream adapter, the explained operation-sequence example, and all three constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064521034. Its size, deque, total, append, conditional popleft, subtraction, and division logic align exactly with the protected app-local class; the list-comprehension solve dispatcher is the sole substantive adapter.

The corrected legal tiers use 128, 1,024, and 8,192 calls with window capacities 64, 512, and the source maximum 1,000; they span 64x and exercise both filling and expiration. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.00 relative growth and 0.99x; correct per-call window recomputation passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.21 and 1.77x.

The Approach accurately derives FIFO expiration and the synchronized running-sum invariant, traces the source example's first expiration, and states O(1) per call, O(m) total time, and O(size) storage.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the sole source example and its complete step-by-step explanation, all constructor and method semantics, and all three source constraints.
